info.album: The Air That I Breathe - The Very Best of the Hollies

podcast.body: This 1972 song by The Hollies was deemed too similar to Radiohead's "Creep" in a subsequent copyright infringement lawsuit. As a result of the legal action, the songwriters, Albert Hammond Sr. and Mike Hazelwood, were granted 25% of the writing credit for "Creep." "It was determined that Creepe sounded way too similar to a 1972 song called The Air That I Breathe."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This 1972 song was the subject of an infringement claim against Radiohead's "Creep." The co-writers of "The Air That I Breathe," Mike Hazelwood and Albert Hammond, were subsequently added to the songwriting credits for "Creep." "was judged to have infringed upon a 1972 song called The Air That I Breathe by the Hollies?"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: The composers of "The Air that I Breathe" successfully sued Radiohead, claiming melodic similarities with Radiohead's 1993 song "Creep," leading to them receiving songwriting credits and a share of the royalties from "Creep." One of the composers is the father of Albert Hammond Jr. of The Strokes. "Radiohead was sued by the Hawley's over Creep because of certain melodic similarities to the 1974 song Be Air that I Breathe."
